meta.title: World Bible (working draft)
meta.scope: World building is largely complete. Game lore is now being defined, starting with a high-level skeleton (see game_lore). Details of each pending piece come next.
notes_for_llm: Treat everything in canon_key.user_decided as fixed canon. Do not contradict it.
Treat everything in canon_key.provisional_elements as proposals the author may change. Stay consistent with them unless told otherwise.
Anything in open_items is undecided. Offer options and ask the author instead of silently inventing.
Tone is a realistic medieval world that is not dark. Hardship exists but is not graphic or grim.
meta.world_name_note: Means the Made Land in the old tongue the gods taught (provisional). Alternatives considered: Solmara, Caelmere, Orvaine.

user_decided: Realistic medieval world, not dark. No vague invented races.

Peoples: human, elf (high, wood, dark), dwarf, high orc, angel, demon, devil, succubus and incubus, vampire, gods and goddesses, their half-races (half-elf etc.), half-animal races with maximum human features (fox, wolf, bunny, lizard, dragon, bear, dog, cat), plus ordinary animals and animal monsters.
Four full societies: human, elf, dwarf, demon.
Different religions with gods and goddesses. No holy days system.
A medieval-style slave system exists: legal in some realms, frowned upon in others.
Several continents. Peoples mostly live separately, with a few big cosmopolitan cities.
An adventurer system exists.
A class/job system (Paths) that is optional, awakened by different means, with some Paths easier for certain races.
A reputation/infamy system and a bounty system.
A supreme non-physical creator god made the world and also made the current physical gods and goddesses.
Gods and angels live on floating islands above each of their major churches.
Demons have their own continent and society.
No separate planes: a two-tier world (ground and god islands). People with very high divinity and power can go to the god islands. No invitation or ascension mechanic.
After death there is nothing.
Every being has magic power (MP) and all magic comes from it.
Calendar: 365 days, 12 months, 7-day week, 4 seasons (summer, rainy, winter, spring).
Half-races are discriminated against, but not everywhere. Relations between races are very frowned upon.
One common currency worldwide. Each major city has its own banks. Various trade houses exist.
One common language worldwide.

Going with: everyone has MP as life-energy and Awakening shapes it into skills; each major people descends from or was shaped by a physical god; the creator is nameless with no temples or clergy; gods seldom descend and angels act as envoys; no resurrection, no ghosts or undead, vampires are living beings.
There is no such thing as interrace marriage anywhere. Half-races are generally born to eloped couples, captive or bonded couples, slave mothers and similar cases.
A god can be killed.
Angels were created by the supreme creator, not by the gods. There are 10 to 20 angels for each god.
Game premise: a man in his 30s from present-day Earth is transported into this world.
Teleportation is allowed. Areas guarded by magic runes (wards) make teleportation to or from them fail.
Mind control is possible, but very expensive and it also tolls the user.
Gunpowder is present. Basic technology like cannons exists, but magic far outperforms it. It is used when magic is expensive.
The game lore skeleton has 6 acts and 25 side characters.
Varan was not killed but enslaved: someone has enslaved the goddess.
Transport: the player simply wakes up in the world, no reason given at the start.
Only cannons, no crude hand firearms.
Protagonist: player chooses name, background, and class/job; skills follow the class.
Side character stories to be decided after main lore is finalised.
Relationship system: as per the game's standard system, no explicit requirement.
Varan is now a goddess named Varan. She was not killed but secretly enslaved and removed from her island 22 years ago. This is the central secret of the game.
The player simply wakes up in Verendel. No explanation is given at the start.
The player chooses their own name, background, and class/job. Skills follow the chosen class.
Only cannons exist. No hand firearms.
Endings are built around gods/goddesses, law, and the player's choice of power, not slavery/peoples axes.
A True Bad End exists where Varan is killed during a failed rescue.
A Power End exists where the player enslaves Varan himself.
A Secret End exists tied to fully resolving the Seekers thread.
Kharrath and his church (the Ember Conclave) enslaved Varan to drain her MP and feed it into Kharrath's power, with the goal of absorbing all gods and becoming the sole deity.
The six acts each protect one god/goddess per act (Acts 2-4), with Act 1 being the longest discovery act and Act 5 being the final confrontation.
Morvane and the Ledger Courts are operational tools of Kharrath's church, not the mastermind.
Malvek did not know about Varan's enslavement and turns ally when exposed.
Nyxara suspects something is wrong with Kharrath but cannot prove it.
Act 1 is the longest act covering Tessara and all of Aldermere.
Power End: the player enslaves all six goddesses and seals all three gods, then rules as the sole power above all of Verendel.
Hestrel and Solenne are also targeted by Kharrath, in Act 5.
Nyxara, after suspecting her bonded partner and confronting him directly at the start of Act 5, is enslaved by Kharrath. The player witnesses it or arrives too late.
Kharrath's full target order: Varan (Act 1 discovery), Aeloria (Act 2), Thessaly (Act 3), Durgrim (Act 4), then Hestrel, Nyxara and Solenne all in Act 5.
All 25 side characters are female.
Queen Maren II's husband King-Consort Aldus Kess is alive.
Queen Ilvariel's husband Lord-Consort Aendrel Vael (wood elf) is alive.
Sylvaris Orenn is a widow; her husband died in the Age of Crowns over 600 years ago.
Four supporting sub-quest characters added: Rina Brightbrush, Kessa Emberscale, Sera Ash, Lady Velura Lysmere.
These four have no act-progression role but are needed for individual character sub-quests.
9-act structure with 9-10 quests in Act 1 and 6-7 per other act.
Each character has an introduction quest before any story-gate quests.
Gate checks are marked as GATE with placeholder conditions to be defined later.
Act 8 has two player-choice tracks: rescue (Ashvault) or confrontation (Emberspire).
Act 9 is a short epilogue showing the world one season after Act 8, with scenes per character relationship.
No retries anywhere. Every failure is a consequence that reshapes the world. Player always moves forward.
Act 1 failures are silent long-game penalties, not immediate blockers.
Acts 2-5: each goddess lost triggers a specific world change and a salvage path in a later act, not an immediate terminus.
Act 6: Nyxara's enslavement is unavoidable. The act gate is Evara (rescue method) and Velindra's warning (coalition strength).
Act 8 difficulty is shaped by how many goddesses were saved across Acts 2-5 and 7. No retry on the final fight.
Narrative defeat sequence exists for players who lose the Act 8 fight after accumulating multiple goddess losses.

Quest details added: each quest has objective, outcome, failure consequence, and failure system link. Goddess target order corrected: Durgrim=Act3, Thessaly=Act4. Two salvage quests added in Act 5 for Aeloria and Thessaly failure paths.
The god-level rune-ward and devil contract mechanism for enslaving goddesses is removed entirely.
Kharrath uses the world's existing slavery system, scaled to divine levels using enormous MP drawn directly from himself.
Kharrath keeps enslaved goddesses compliant through binding and carnal pleasure.
The slavery mechanism is the same in kind as mortal slavery; only the scale (MP cost) and the target (divine beings) are extraordinary.

Character psychology layer added: each of the 25 main side characters has personality traits, humor style, baseline trust and loyalty, jealousy tendency, affection style, and sexual psychology (confidence, lean, resistance profile, hidden desire).

cosmology.creator: Non-physical supreme god. Made the world, the sky, the First Wyrms (great dragons), the wild beasts, the eight physical gods and the angels, then withdrew. Nameless, no temples or clergy. All faiths acknowledge it.

gods.nature: Physical beings made by the creator, in four bonded pairs
gods.involvement: Seldom descend. Act through angels, blessings, omens and chosen followers.
gods.mortality: Gods do not age but can be killed.

kharrath_target_order.act: enslaved before game starts, discovered Act 1
Act 5 threat (ward half-built from Durgrim components)
Act 6, enslaved when she confronts Kharrath directly mid-act
Act 7 threat, final target before the confrontation

status.note: Only Malvek, Aeloria, Thessaly and Durgrim are free and available as allies in Act 5. Hestrel, Nyxara and Solenne are all at risk simultaneously.

enslaved.held_at: Ashvault, Vashkar — in physical captivity within the Ember Temple's deepest level
enslaved.enslaver: Kharrath, using the world's slavery system at divine scale
enslaved.mechanism: Enslaved using the same system as mortal slavery, but powered by Kharrath's own MP at an enormous cost. Binding and carnal pleasure keep her compliant rather than resistant.
enslaved.note: Alive and aware. Her MP has been draining into Kharrath for 22 years. She is conscious but does not fight the compliance.

status.nyxara_note: Enslaved mid-Act 6 by the same method. Kharrath's bonded partner. Aware and compliant.

pairs.note: A triple bonding. One of three pairs and one triple, the only such group.

gods.sex_count: 6 goddesses (Solenne, Varan, Aeloria, Thessaly, Hestrel, Nyxara) and 3 gods (Durgrim, Malvek, Kharrath). The Creator made six goddesses and three gods; no one knows why.

angels.origin: Created by the supreme creator, not by the gods, and assigned to serve the gods.
angels.numbers: 10 to 20 angels for each god, so roughly 80 to 160 in total
angels.role: Live with their god on the island and act as envoys.
angels.mortality: Do not age but can be killed. Death is final and no new angels are created (provisional), so each loss is permanent.

cosmology.islands: A floating island hangs above each god's major church. The city beneath it is a pilgrimage site.
cosmology.planes: None. Two-tier world: the ground and the god islands.
cosmology.death: Nothing follows death. No afterlife, no resurrection, no ghosts, no undead. Memory Halls keep names and deeds.
cosmology.divinity: Purity and strength of a being's MP, sharpened by faith, deeds and Path mastery. Very high divinity and power lets a being reach the god islands.
cosmology.common_tongue: A gift of the gods. One language worldwide. Accents, idioms, scripts and naming traditions still differ by people.

calendar.reckoning: YC = Year of the Charter. Year 0 is the founding of the Wayfarers' Charter. Current year about 614 YC (provisional).
calendar.week_rhythm: Five work days, then Market Day, then Restday. Restday is a day off, not a holy day (provisional).

magic.source: Every being has MP. All magic comes from MP.
magic.baseline: MP quietly powers strength, health and endurance for everyone (provisional).
magic.awakening_meaning: Awakening is the ability to shape MP into skills (provisional).
magic.pool_by_people: Humans, orcs and dwarves around average. High elves, dark elves, demons, devils and vampires higher. Angels far above. Gods beyond measure.
magic.recovery: A night's rest and food restore most of a pool.
casting_types: ritual (slow, can be done by a group)
magic.overdraw: Casting beyond your pool drains vitality and can cause collapse. Repeated overdraw causes burnout, a lasting loss of pool.
magic.divine_magic: Blessings are the god's will, but the cleric's own MP powers them.
limits: No scrying beyond line of sight except limited Oracle visions

rules: Anyone with MP can trigger an enchanted item, even without a Path
Monster parts retain MP, which makes them valuable to Runesmiths and Alchemists

magic.detection: Awakened people can sense MP at close range.
magic.regulation: Kingdoms regulate battle magic inside cities. The Arcane Collegium licenses mages.
magic.death: MP dissipates at death. Nothing remains.

teleportation.wards: Areas guarded by magic runes make teleportation to or from them fail (user decided).
teleportation.who: Awakened with a spatial Arcane ability, rare even among the Awakened (provisional)
teleportation.cost: Scales with distance and the number of people carried. Usually a large share of the caster's pool (provisional).
teleportation.destination: Must be a place the caster has visited or one marked by an anchor rune (provisional)
teleportation.ward_upkeep: Wards are engraved by Runesmiths and powered by stored MP, so large wards are expensive and limited to key sites (provisional).
teleportation.effects: Ordinary travel still dominates because teleporting is costly and rare (provisional).

mind_control.status: Possible but very expensive, and it tolls the user too (user decided)
mind_control.cost: Extreme MP cost plus backlash on the caster: lost vitality and a risk of lasting burnout, growing with the target's resistance (provisional).
mind_control.duration: Short, and a target with a much larger pool can resist or break it (provisional).
mind_control.who: Rare, Adept tier or higher, usually Pact, Enchanter or Emissary Paths (provisional)
mind_control.cheap_version: Charm and persuasion only influence and cost little.
mind_control.law: A grave crime in most realms (provisional).
mind_control.slavery_note: Too costly to use as a basis for slavery or armies, but usable on single high-value targets (provisional).

peoples.path_affinity: Martial, Craft, any by training. Most flexible, no edge.
peoples.notes: Most numerous, politically divided, short-lived compared to elves.
Long-lived. Some alive today remember the Age of Voyages.
Clan-based, keeps distance from the court.

peoples.origin: Split from the high elven court in a succession crisis during the Age of Crowns
peoples.notes: Merchant-and-spy dynasties. Rivals of high elves, not villains.
Clan and guild based. Oaths and debts are sacred.
Clan society. Raids and captives are part of frontier life.
They are people, not animals. Enslaving or hunting them is a serious crime in most realms.

peoples.origin: Claim descent from the First Wyrms (provisional)
peoples.notes: A beastfolk people, distinct from true dragons.
House-based society built on bloodline and contracts.
Contract and law bound. Run the Ledger Courts.
Living beings, long-lived bloodline, a small old aristocracy. Not undead.

peoples.origin: Created by the supreme creator, 10 to 20 for each god
peoples.notes: Serve the gods and act as envoys. Rarely on the ground. Very few exist, so each one matters.
Eight physical beings. They do not age but can be killed. See religion.gods.

half_races.rule: Offspring of two peoples (half-elf, half-orc, half-demon, half-angel, etc.). They inherit a blend of both parents' Path affinities.
half_races.no_interrace_marriage: No legal or customary interrace marriage exists anywhere. Unions between peoples are unrecognised and no faith performs the rite for a mixed couple.
how_born: Eloped couples who flee their peoples, often to borderlands or cosmopolitan cities
Captive or bonded couples, where an enslaved or captive person and an owner or captor form a lasting bond. Morally tangled, because the power gap makes it unclear how free the choice was.
Enslaved mothers, whose children are born into the same legal status where slavery is legal
Frontier and trade-road liaisons among soldiers, caravan crews and adventurers, often unacknowledged
Rarely, liaisons with angels or god-touched beings
half_races.legal_status_rule: The child takes the mother's people and legal status, unless the father formally acknowledges and frees them (provisional).
half_races.lifespan_rule: Falls between the parents' lifespans, leaning toward the shorter-lived parent. A half-elf with a human parent often lives 150 to 250 years.
half_races.fertility_rule: Any two humanoid peoples can conceive, but odds fall as the lifespan gap and lineage distance grow, so half-races are few. Peoples shaped by the same god or pair are closest.

map.notes: Free if the mother is free, but barred from noble rank and temple posts
Chivalric culture gives them more room
Status follows the mother, so many are enslaved
Cannot inherit, but can be freed with protections
Barred from Court rank, allowed only as commoners
Useful as go-betweens, excluded from house rank
Cannot be clan-kin, only hearth-guests in guilds
Commons by default, but a strong bloodline can be adopted by a House by contract
Accepted if the father acknowledges the child at the clan fire
Couples live openly but cannot wed

half_races.inter_race_relations: Very frowned upon everywhere. No interrace marriage exists.

continents.character: Ancient forests, white-stone courts, twilight canyons in the west
Mountain ranges, deep holds, iron and gold
Warm volcanic highlands, red-stone cities, fertile ash-soil valleys. Vivid, not grim.
Steppes, savanna, jungle, marsh, river deltas, mountains

cosmopolitan_cities.location: Concord Isle, center of the Middle Sea
cosmopolitan_cities.notes: Founded the Charter. Neutral charter city.

cosmopolitan_cities.location: River crossroads between Aldermere and Sylvaren
Mountain pass between Khardun and Aldermere
cosmopolitan_cities.notes: Toll disputes settled by the Charter.
Demons, dark elves and vampires trade here.

layout.gloam_strait: Narrow strait between Sylvaren and Vashkar, home to Gloamhaven

sylvaren.terrain: Vast forests, moonlit lakes, twilight canyons in the west
sylvaren.ancient_site: The Dawnstones, a circle from the Age of Dawn

khardun.terrain: Mountain ranges, deep valleys, hot springs
khardun.ancient_site: The First Hold, a sealed ancient hall

vashkar.climate: Warm, with a fierce rainy season

tharos.ancient_site: The Wyrm Graves, bones of a First Wyrm

travel.note: All provisional. Teleportation exists but is costly and rare, so ordinary travel still dominates.

aldermere.binding_body: Diet of Crowns. Settles disputes between crowns but has little power to enforce.

realms.notes: Richest farmland, most prestigious crown. No clear heir. Hosts Solenne's Dawn Cathedral.
Cold northern highlands, devout, law-bound. Hosts Varan's Crown Basilica.

realms.slavery: Legal, with formal protections and manumission traditions

realms.ruler: Queen Ilvariel the Unforgotten and the Council of Elders
Council of house-heads: Ysmere (trade), Kaelthorn (craft), Vesh (information)

khardun.ruler: High King Haldrek Stonevow, chosen by the Moot of Thanes

Largest mining and smithing hold. Hestrel's Great Forge.
Frontier hold guarding the human border.

vashkar.ruler: Archduchess Vesperine Kaldrith, chosen by the Conclave of the Great Houses

houses.role: Devil-aligned, runs the Ledger Courts at Ashvault (Malvek's Hall of Ledgers)
Succubi and incubi courtiers and envoys

regions.organisation: Clans (Ironjaw, Redhorn, Ashfang) under a Warmother's Council

tharos.notes: Thessaly's Hunt-Mother's Lodge stands at Wildmark, where clans gather for seasonal moots.

beastfolk_lands.name: Ashkor Emberscale

stormvale.goal: Secure the sea lanes and ease Hallowmere's tolls

marrowen.goal: Protect slavery in law and expand southern influence

human.government: Feudal monarchies, loosely tied by the Diet of Crowns
human.law: Three overlapping court systems: royal, church and guild
human.economy: Farming, wool, timber, trade. Guilds control the towns.
human.military: Feudal levies, knightly orders, mercenary companies

high_elf.government: Monarch and Council of Elders, advised by Loremasters
high_elf.culture: Decades-long apprenticeships, rare and celebrated births, sacred memory and lineage. Politics is slow and grudges last generations.

wood_elf.notes: Keep their distance from the court.

dark_elf.government: Council of house-heads from Ysmere (trade and banking), Kaelthorn (craft) and Vesh (information)
dark_elf.culture: Dusk-and-night cycle, markets open at twilight, favors are the real currency. Discretion and house loyalty are sacred.
dark_elf.economy: Underground trade, banking, crafts and information
dark_elf.slavery: Chattel banned. Indenture is term-limited and registered in a ledger (provisional).
dark_elf.rivalry: High elves see them as defectors. They see the high elves as frozen in the past.

dwarf.government: High King chosen by the Moot of Thanes. Each hold run by its clan council.
dwarf.law: The Ledger records oaths and debts. Breaking an oath is the gravest crime. Chattel slavery banned, term-limited debt-bondage allowed.
dwarf.economy: Mining, smithing, stonework, runecraft. Guilds control quality and export.

demon.government: Conclave of the Great Houses, led by an Archduke chosen from among them
demon.devils: A law-bound order running the Ledger Courts, the contract-enforcing bureaucracy
demon.succubi_incubi: Organised into courtly houses of diplomats, negotiators and envoys
demon.culture: Status comes from contracts kept, favors owed, and family name. Colourful and politically sharp, not grim.

high_orc.government: Warmother's Council of clan matriarchs, with a warchief leading each clan in war
high_orc.culture: Mounted nomads who breed horses and warg mounts. Status comes from deeds, disputes are settled by trial of combat, guests are sacred.
high_orc.captives: Under kin-right, a captive who serves a year and a day can be adopted into the clan (provisional).

beastfolk.government: No single ruler. Each region has a clan council. The Moot-Caller convenes all of them at Wildmark.

regions.fangwood: Wolf, bear and dog pack-clans. Deeds above rank.
regions.reedmarsh: Lizard villages with healers and ritualists
regions.burrow_commons: Bunny warrens with communal property, scouts and messengers
regions.red_glades: Fox clans as brokers and traders
regions.scaled_peaks: Dragonkin clans who guard family hoards and keep wyrm-speaker elders

beastfolk.status: They are people. Enslaving one is a crime almost everywhere. In cosmopolitan cities they work as scouts, guides and traders.

angel.nature: Created by the supreme creator and assigned to serve a god. Each god has its own host of 10 to 20.
angel.structure: Hosts are small, so most ranks have only a few angels each (provisional).
angel.culture: Duty and service. Rare trips to the ground on missions. Each host takes on the character of its god.
angel.mortality: Can be killed. Death is final and no new angels are created (provisional).

vampire.structure: No realm. Advisors, physicians, bankers and scholars inside other peoples' courts. Status by age.
vampire.council: The Quiet Table, a council of elders that settles disputes between vampires across continents (provisional)
vampire.law: Feeding on the unwilling is a capital crime. Blood comes from paid donors in licensed blood-houses.

devil.government: Run the Ledger Courts of Ashvault
devil.culture: Exact and literal. They never lie but do not volunteer information.
devil.contracts: A sealed contract binds the signer's MP and breaking it drains it (provisional).
devil.role: Neutral arbiters for international contracts. The Charter often hires them.

religion.structure: Four faiths, eight gods in four bonded pairs. Each god has one major church and one floating island above it, plus a host of angels. Because death is final, religion is about this life: blessings, guidance, law, and heritage. No holy days system.

faiths.character: Mercy and law. Varan's church controls coronations, Solenne's runs hospitals.
Nature, moon, hunt and kin. Strict on bloodline purity among elves.
Oaths, craft and ancestral memory. Strict on bloodline purity.

faiths.followers: Demons, devils, succubi and incubi, vampires, dark elves
faiths.character: Ambition, fire, conquest, freedom and binding contracts. The Night Court covers all three gods of the demon peoples.

gods.name: Solenne
gods.title: Goddess of Dawn and Mercy
gods.symbol: Rising sun over an open hand
orders: Order of the Open Hand (healers and hospitals)
gods.on_slavery: Preaches mercy and urges manumission, does not forbid it
gods.on_half_races: Welcoming in principle, inconsistent in practice
gods.status: Alive but silent and grieving for Varan, her bonded partner (provisional).

gods.name: Varan
gods.title: Goddess of Law and Kings
gods.on_slavery: Upholds the law as written and regulates it
gods.status: Enslaved by Kharrath in 592 YC using the world's slavery system at divine scale. Held in physical captivity in Ashvault's deepest level. Conscious and aware but kept compliant through binding and carnal pleasure. Her MP drains into Kharrath.
gods.angel_host_status: The Crownhost is scattered. Some dead, some missing. A few walk the ground searching for her, sensing she is alive but cannot locate her.
gods.paths_note: Templar and oath-bound Knight Paths can no longer be awakened through Varan's Temple Rite — her island is dark and her divine authority is being drained. Existing holders keep their Paths.

gods.name: Aeloria
gods.title: Goddess of Forests and the Moon

gods.name: Thessaly
gods.title: The Hunt-Mother
gods.on_slavery: Forbids enslaving beastfolk. Orc captives are usually adopted into clans.

gods.name: Durgrim
gods.title: The Stonefather
gods.sacred_animal: Stone-goat (honored as a symbol, not as living ancestors)
gods.on_slavery: Bans chattel slavery, allows term-limited debt-bondage

gods.name: Nyxara
gods.title: Goddess of Night and Desire
orders: The Velvet Houses (tied to House Lysmere)
gods.on_slavery: Favors personal freedom, tolerates bondage by contract
gods.act_5_fate: Confronts Kharrath at the start of Act 6 and is enslaved by him using the same method as Varan. The player witnesses it. This is the emotional turning point of the final act.

gods.name: Malvek
gods.title: God of Contracts and Bargains
gods.on_slavery: Contract-bondage is sacred and strictly enforced
gods.on_half_races: Judged by the contract they hold

gods.name: Kharrath
gods.title: God of War, Conquest, and Fire
orders: The Ember Conclave (inner circle, knows the truth)
gods.on_slavery: Conquest is natural. The strong own the weak.
gods.status: Active and growing stronger by siphoning Varan's MP. The central villain of the game.
gods.secret: Has enslaved Varan and plans to absorb all other gods to become the sole deity of Verendel.
gods.note: Nyxara suspects something is wrong but cannot prove it.
gods.slavery_method: Uses the world's existing slavery system scaled to divine levels, powered by his own MP. Compliance maintained through binding and carnal pleasure. Each enslaved goddess's drained MP reduces the cost of the next enslavement.

church_leaders.title: Lord Justiciar
church_leaders.name: Corvin Ashgrove
church_leaders.note: Leads the church of an enslaved goddess. May know the truth behind the Silence (provisional).

religion.faith_strain: The Radiant Faith is strained: Solenne is silent, Varan's church keeps up the official line, and some clergy demand answers.

status_tiers: indentured servants working off a term

by_realm.southern_human: Legal and common (Marrowen). Sarrakesh: legal with formal protections.
by_realm.northern_human: Restricted to debt bondage with fixed terms (Aurendale, Hallowmere, Stormvale). Castellane frowns on it.
by_realm.orc_clans: War captives, often adopted into the clan over time
by_realm.high_elves: Banned, though quiet exploitation of outsiders exists
by_realm.beastfolk: Enslaving beastfolk is a crime almost everywhere.

slavery.origin: Grew from captives and debts in the Age of Crowns. The Charter treaty left the question to each realm, which is why the world is a patchwork.
slavery.story_engine: Smuggling, border disputes, escaped slaves seeking sanctuary, rival legal codes, and awakened people discovering their Path while in bondage.
slavery.awakened_and_slavery: Some realms free or buy out the Awakened, some bind them with legal contracts, some forbid owning one.
slavery.birth_status: The child of an enslaved mother takes her legal status where slavery is legal, unless the father formally acknowledges and frees the child.

divine_slavery.mechanism: The world's existing slavery system applied to divine beings. MP-intensive for the enslaver.
divine_slavery.compliance_method: Binding and carnal pleasure rather than punishment or suppression.
divine_slavery.note: The same framework that enslaves mortals can, in principle, be applied to any being with MP — including gods. Kharrath is simply the first to have enough MP to attempt it on a divine being.

economy.currency: Concord Crown, one currency worldwide, minted by the Concord Mint and licensed city banks to a single standard (provisional name)
economy.banking_rules: Each major city has its own banks. Banks issue letters of credit honored by other banks. Loans run 10 to 20 percent a year. Unpaid debt can lead to debt bondage.
dues: temple tithe of about a tenth
road and bridge tolls (Stonebridge is the famous one)
economy.resources: Hides, scales, tusks (Craft), venom and bile (Alchemists), bones and horns (Runesmiths), trophies (Proof of Deed bounties). Overhunting causes regulation.
regulated_goods: gunpowder (sulfur from Vashkar, saltpeter from caves)

adventurer_system.organisation: The Wayfarers' Charter, an international guild founded in Concord. Its license is recognised across borders and grants travel, arms and contract rights almost everywhere.
adventurer_system.joining: A trial at any guild hall, sponsored by a licensed member or local authority
adventurer_system.services: Lodging, gear storage at member rates, healers, item identification. The guild takes a cut.
adventurer_system.jurisdiction: Limited legal protection. Kingdoms still apply local law.
adventurer_system.link_to_paths: Wayfarer rank and Path tier are separate but loosely correlated.

methods.how: A priest performs a rite at a shrine and the god answers or does not
methods.note: Varan's rite no longer works since 592 YC, so Templar and oath-bound Knight Paths can no longer be awakened this way.

methods.how: Years of training end in a formal trial (duel, forge-test, vigil)
Latent inheritance wakes at coming-of-age or in a crisis
Bargain with a spirit, devil, angel or ancient being
Living in tune with nature, beasts or ancestral memory
Rare crystals sold by the Charter that nudge a ready person over the line
methods.difficulty: Expensive, only works if already close

methods.how: Rare, unpredictable awakening in a crisis

paths.affinity_rule: Affinity makes a Path easier or faster for a people. It is never a hard restriction. See peoples[].path_affinity.

reputation_and_bounty.principle: News travels slowly. Reputation is local first, then spreads via heralds, bards, merchant caravans, ship crews, temple messengers, and the Charter's Ledger of Names.

tracks.renown: How widely you are known and admired
tracks.infamy: How widely you are known for wrongdoing
tracks.standing: Relationship with a specific faction, realm, temple, guild or House

reputation_and_bounty.same_act_different_realm: Acts are judged by local law and values, by witnesses, location and who was harmed. Example: freeing a slave is theft in southern human realms, honorable among high elves, a breach of contract in demon houses.
reputation_and_bounty.weregild: Blood-price paid to a victim's family as an alternative to punishment. Recognised by dwarves and northern humans.

issuers: Wayfarers' Charter (monsters and its own rogue members)
rules: Posted on boards in towns, guild halls and temples
Legally valid only in the issuing realm unless extradition or Charter sanction applies
Reward grows with infamy tier and target danger
Rewards can include land, minor titles, pardons or favors

reputation_and_bounty.teleportation_and_fugitives: Fugitives who can teleport are rare. Prisons, courthouses and borders use ward runes, and bounty hunters rely on trackers and warded ground (provisional).

bestiary.note: Beastfolk are people, not animals. Monsters are treated as dangerous wildlife with habitats and diets, not as evil. Tiers match Wayfarer ranks.
bestiary.mounts_and_companions: Hounds, hawks and horses are common. Griffons, hippogriffs and tamed wyverns are rare and usually need a Beastbinder or Ranger Path. Many kingdoms require a Charter license or noble permit for dangerous mounts.
bestiary.not_included: Undead and horror creatures. No ghosts or undead exist in this world.

biology.note: All ages are provisional. Adulthood is 18 or older for every people.

human.lifespan: 60 to 80, many die earlier from disease and war

high_elf.notes: Rare births, youthful for centuries, slender with keen sight

dark_elf.notes: Eyes adapted to low light, poor in bright glare

dwarf.notes: Few children per lifetime. Short, broad, dense-boned.

beastfolk.notes: Human build with animal ears, tail and species traits. Fur or scale patches. Senses tuned to the species.

succubus_incubus.notes: Youthful for long. Charm is an inherent MP trait (provisional).

vampire.notes: Living beings who can die from wounds or illness. Need small amounts of blood for MP upkeep, taken from paid donors in licensed blood-houses. Feeding on the unwilling is a capital crime everywhere. Prolonged daylight saps their MP.

angel.notes: Created by the supreme creator, not born. Can be killed and death is final. Roughly 80 to 160 exist in total. Liaisons with mortals are extremely rare, so half-angels are almost unheard of.

god.notes: Can be killed. Killing a god would be catastrophic for its faith, its island and its people.

human.food: Bread, stew, ale, wine in the south
human.dress_and_homes: Wool and linen. Timber and stone homes, castles and walled towns
human.customs: Dowries and bride-prices. Guild and parish life
human.naming: Given name plus family or place name, e.g. Edric of Solhaven

high_elf.food: Fruit, honeyed bread, tea, light wines
high_elf.customs: Long courtships. Music and poetry. Heavy etiquette
high_elf.naming: Given name plus house or deed-name, e.g. Ilvariel of Silver Dawn

dark_elf.food: Mushroom dishes, spiced wine, river fish
dark_elf.dress_and_homes: Dark layered cloth in muted colors. Carved cave-cities

dwarf.food: Roast meat, dark bread, strong beer
dwarf.dress_and_homes: Leather and mail. Carved stone halls
dwarf.customs: Oath-swearing. Craft pride. Beards braided with clan marks
dwarf.naming: Given name plus clan name, e.g. Haldrek Stonevow

high_orc.customs: Horse-games, trial by combat, open hearth hospitality
high_orc.naming: Given name, clan, and a deed, e.g. Gorra Redhorn the Horse-Breaker

beastfolk.food: Species-based, from grain and fruit to fish and game
beastfolk.dress_and_homes: Light practical clothes that accommodate ears and tails
beastfolk.customs: Pack and clan feasts. Seasonal moots at Wildmark

demon.food: Spiced meats, fire-roasted dishes, sweet liquors
demon.customs: Contracts at every occasion. Courtly dueling
demon.naming: Given name plus house name, e.g. Vesperine Kaldrith

culture.marriage: Only within a people. Courtship, dowries or bride-prices, and a simple hearth-rite in the local temple.
culture.death_customs: Because nothing follows death, funerals focus on legacy. Names and deeds are carved in Memory Halls and written in family Deedbooks.
culture.literacy: Common among clergy, guilds, nobles and elves. Rarer among peasants (roughly one in five humans).
culture.education: Apprenticeships, temple schools, guild halls, and the Arcane Collegium of Tessara.

military_and_technology.tech_level: Late medieval. Iron, steel and plate for elites. Longbows and crossbows, trebuchets, siege towers, sailing ships, water mills, basic clockwork. Gunpowder exists (user decided): basic technology like cannons, but magic far outperforms it. Books are hand-copied. Letters travel by messenger, signal fire and Charter relay. Magic adds enchanted gear and healing, both rare. Teleportation exists but is costly and rare.

forces.human: Feudal levies, knights, crossbow companies, mercenaries
forces.high_elf: Wardens (rangers and archers) and the elite Sunlit Guard
forces.cannon_crews: Siege and fortress cannon crews in human and dwarven armies (provisional)

military_and_technology.war_rules: Armies are small and campaigns are limited by the rainy season. The Charter bars attacks on temples and Memory Halls. Fortresses are warded against teleportation (provisional).

gunpowder.status: Present. Cannons and similar basic technology. Magic far outperforms it. Used when magic is expensive (user decided).
gunpowder.use: Mainly in sieges, fortresses and on ships, and by realms short on mages or when MP is exhausted, such as long sieges and mass levies (provisional).
gunpowder.limits: Slow reload, loud and unreliable. No reliable hand firearms yet (provisional).
gunpowder.production: Sulfur from Vashkar's volcanoes, saltpeter from caves. Cannons cast by dwarven smiths and human guilds (provisional).
gunpowder.regulation: Gunpowder is a regulated trade good (provisional).

healers.temples: The Order of the Open Hand runs hospitals and treats the poor

by_people.dwarf: Hold-surgeons are best with wounds and bones

medicine.healing_magic: Cleric Path heals by speeding natural recovery using MP from both healer and patient. Closes wounds and mends bones in days. Cannot regrow lost limbs, reverse aging or revive the dead. Large heals leave the patient exhausted.

diseases.notes: Contagious fever and rash. Survivors are immune.
Dysentery from bad water, common in armies and ships
Miners' wasting lung, especially in Khardun
Rare epidemic that returns every few decades

medicine.susceptibility: Elves resist common illness, dwarves resist poison, humans are most vulnerable.
other: Childbirth is the leading cause of death among humans
Alchemists make antidotes for monster venom

bounty_hunters.who: Licensed Charter hunter, Journeyman or higher
bounty_hunters.method: By the book. Brings targets in alive and follows jurisdiction.

bounty_hunters.who: Local deputy for a reeve or sheriff
bounty_hunters.method: Knows the streets. Sometimes takes bribes.

bounty_hunters.who: Crown Templar tracking heretics and desecrators
bounty_hunters.method: Zealous but lawful. Hunts for the temple.
Takes any contract. Skilled, flexible morals.

bounty_hunters.who: Devil agent of the Ledger Courts
Orc or beastfolk, often Wild Lodge
bounty_hunters.method: Hunts poachers and killers of sacred animals
Legal in Marrowen and Sarrakesh, hated and often outlawed elsewhere. Natural enemy of the Free Road.

bounty_hunters.who: Monster specialist, often Ranger or Beastbinder

bounty_hunters.method: Does not fight. Locates fugitives for a fee.

central_mystery.event: Varan, Goddess of Law and Kings, was secretly enslaved in 592 YC by Kharrath's Ember Conclave. She is alive and held in a rune-ward vault beneath Ashvault. Her MP is being drained into Kharrath.
central_mystery.truth: Kharrath enslaved Varan using the world's own slavery system, scaled to divine levels by drawing on his own MP at enormous cost. Morvane's Ember Conclave managed the physical capture operation — agents subdued Varan at the moment of maximum vulnerability and Kharrath bound her himself. He keeps her and all subsequent enslaved goddesses compliant through binding and carnal pleasure rather than through pain or force.
central_mystery.perpetrator: Kharrath, God of War, through his Ember Conclave inner circle
central_mystery.motive: Drain the other gods' MP to grow strong enough to absorb all of them and become the sole deity of Verendel, equal to or replacing the Creator.
central_mystery.malvek_note: Malvek unknowingly helped design the containment ward, believing it was for a rogue angel. He does not know about Varan.
central_mystery.nyxara_note: Nyxara suspects something is wrong with Kharrath but cannot prove it and fears her own bonded partner.
central_mystery.player_arrival: The corrupted Seekers ritual was not fully controlled. It pulled an unclaimed soul from outside the world. The player is that accident.
god_threat_order: Hestrel (Act 5 threat, ward half-built from Durgrim components)
Nyxara (Act 6, enslaved mid-act when she confronts Kharrath directly)
Solenne (Act 7 final target, simultaneous with coalition assembly)
central_mystery.kharrath_growth: Each captured goddess makes Kharrath stronger and the next capture easier. After 22 years of Varan's MP, he is now measurably stronger than any of the other gods.
central_mystery.nyxara_fate: Nyxara suspects Kharrath from the start but cannot act against her bonded partner. At the start of Act 5 she confronts him directly. He enslaves her on the spot. The player witnesses this or arrives moments too late. This moment makes the final confrontation personal.
central_mystery.act_5_structure: Three simultaneous threats. The player cannot handle all three alone. The coalition (Malvek's church, Aeloria's Silverboughs, Thessaly's Wild Lodge, Durgrim's Oathkeepers, the Charter) each take one target while the player goes for Kharrath and Varan.
central_mystery.kharrath_power_growth: Each enslaved goddess adds to Kharrath's power. If Hestrel, Nyxara or Solenne are captured before the player stops him, he becomes measurably harder to defeat. Capturing all remaining in Act 5 before the player reaches Emberspire triggers the True Bad End.

mechanism.base: The world's existing slavery system — the same legal and physical framework used for mortal slaves, scaled to a divine being.
mechanism.mp_cost: Enormous. Kharrath draws the MP from himself, not from a constructed device. This is why enslaving each successive goddess becomes slightly easier — he feeds on Varan's drained MP to power the next enslavement.
mechanism.compliance: Binding and carnal pleasure. The enslaved goddesses are aware but do not resist. This is more unsettling than a mechanical suppression — they are themselves, but kept compliant.
mechanism.capture_operation: Morvane's Ember Conclave handled physical logistics: isolating each goddess at a moment of vulnerability, bringing Kharrath's agents close enough for him to act. The Seekers' corrupted ritual was used for Varan — it opened access to her island long enough for the capture.
mechanism.drain: Once enslaved, each goddess's MP slowly drains into Kharrath, fuelling his growing power and making the next enslavement cheaper.

central_mystery.what_investigators_find: Without a constructed device or contract, the evidence trail is different. Investigators find: physical evidence of a capture operation (Morvane's logistics), the corrupted Seekers ritual that opened access to Varan's island, the drain on divine MP at each goddess's church, and Kharrath's growing power over 22 years. There is no 'ward' to find and destroy — only a captor to confront and overpower.

game_lore.status: High-level skeleton. Every part except the premise is a proposal.
game_lore.premise: A man in his 30s from present-day Earth is pulled into Verendel, 22 years after Varan was killed.

hook.impossible_arrival: Teleportation exists within the world, but nothing in Verendel's rules allows crossing between worlds. With no separate planes, his arrival from another world should be impossible, which makes it a clue.
hook.foreign_mp: Every being has MP shaped by a god's lineage. His is unattuned, so he has no people affinity and Temple Rites respond to him unpredictably.
hook.outsiders_eye: Modern knowledge gives perspective on slavery, hierarchy and purity laws, not tech cheats. Gunpowder and cannons already exist and magic far outperforms them.

transport_options.idea: The Seekers of the First Word performed a ritual Morvane corrupted. It pulled the player in as an accident. This is the answer.

starting_point.reason: Neutral river city between humans and elves with a Charter hall, the Arcane Collegium and easy roads to every region.

game_lore.central_conflict: Who enslaved Varan, and will another goddess fall? The world is fraying: the Radiant Faith is split, coronations have lost their seal, and the Ledger Courts rise into the vacuum.

acts.name: The Silence
acts.length_note: Longest act. Covers Tessara and all of Aldermere.

quests.name: Eyes Open
quests.objective: Survive the first hour in Tessara: find food, shelter, and someone willing to talk without papers or coin.
quests.outcome: Player learns the world basics: currency, the Charter, the common tongue, and that they are at a crossroads between two peoples. No characters introduced yet.
quests.failure_consequence: If arrested and jailed, the player must talk their way out or break out. No hard failure — the world opens either way.

quests.name: The Examiner's Eye
quests.objective: Pass the three-part Charter entrance trial: combat assessment, contract-reading test, and a judgment scenario.
quests.outcome: Aldra sponsors the player as an Initiate. She becomes the player's first Charter contact and informal mentor.
quests.failure_consequence: Failing the trial means repeating it after completing one open contract as a probationer. Delays Act 1 progress by one quest slot.

quests.name: First Coin
quests.objective: 1.3a: Escort a merchant's cart from Tessara to Brightwater — bandits on the road. 1.3b: Retrieve a stolen ledger from a river gang on the Tessara docks. 1.3c: Track a skip who took a contract fee and vanished.
quests.outcome: Player earns first Marks, builds initial Charter standing, and hears the first background rumour: Hallowmere's Templars are having a quiet crisis that no one will name.
quests.failure_consequence: Each sub-contract can be failed individually. Failed contracts lose pay and reduce Charter standing but do not block the act. A second attempt is available at a 20% fee penalty.

quests.name: Something Wrong With You
quests.objective: Complete Syrael's initial MP assessment at the Collegium. Answer her questions as fully or vaguely as the player chooses. Negotiate the fee upward if desired.
quests.outcome: Syrael begins researching the player's foreign MP. She will surface again in 1.9 with findings. Player earns coin and a standing Collegium invitation.
quests.failure_consequence: Skipping this quest means 1.9 cannot be triggered. Rune-ward theory arrives one act late (Act 3 instead of Act 2), making the Khardun investigation harder.

quests.name: The Road Between
quests.objective: Travel with Mira to Hallowmere via the border roads after the direct road is closed. Pay her a share of the contract fee.
quests.outcome: Mira becomes the player's travel contact and under-road network. She mentions the northern roads have been watched by people who are not bandits and not Charter.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Mira, the player reaches Hallowmere via the long road, losing one quest slot. The under-road network is unavailable until a replacement contact is found in Act 2.

quests.name: The Quiet Templar
quests.objective: Escort Dame Dava Colth to the Monastery of the Crown's Rest. A Templar patrol stops them on the road and clearly knows Dava.
quests.outcome: Player delivers Dava and learns she was the finest Templar in Hallowmere a year ago. The patrol's odd deference signals something unspoken.
quests.failure_consequence: If the escort fails (ambush succeeds), Dava reaches the monastery alone. The second meeting in 1.12 still unlocks but requires the player to seek her out rather than her seeking them.

quests.name: The Varnhold Clerk
quests.objective: Deliver a sealed letter to Varan's Crown Basilica in Varnhold. Notice Edwyn's distress — optional action that unlocks 1.11.
quests.outcome: If the player noticed and asked: Edwyn slips a note into their saddlebag — meet alone after vespers. If they did not notice: Edwyn files the visit and no follow-up is triggered automatically.
quests.failure_consequence: Missing the optional notice means 1.11 never opens. Without Edwyn's records, the Lord Justiciar in Act 7 will not publicly retract the Silence. True End and Secret End are locked.

quests.name: A Queen's Harbour
quests.type: Character introduction — Queen Maren II (7) and Princess Lysa Voss (8)
quests.objective: Security detail for a diplomatic reception aboard Queen Maren's flagship in Port Halcyon. Defuse a diplomatic incident between a Hallowmere envoy and a Stormvale officer without causing a scene.
quests.outcome: Queen Maren gives the player a Charter commendation letter valid at any port. Princess Lysa quietly asks if they have been to Varnhold recently — seeding the correspondence thread.
quests.failure_consequence: If the diplomatic incident is mishandled, Maren does not issue the commendation. Port Halcyon standing is reduced and Lysa does not approach the player this evening — her thread opens one quest later via a letter instead.

quests.name: What You Are
quests.gate: Completing 1.4 and minimum relationship with Syrael [GATE]
quests.objective: Help Syrael petition the Collegium's senior council for restricted archive access via reputation check (Journeyman standing) or a council favour.
quests.outcome: Syrael gets partial access and finds one page describing a ward that suppresses divine MP. She does not yet know what it means. Player has the first theoretical piece of the puzzle.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Journeyman standing or the council favour, access is denied this act. Syrael gains access at the start of Act 2 instead, arriving one act late.

quests.name: The Wanderer at the Docks
quests.objective: Find and engage the woman on the Gullhaven dock. Mention Varan's name (heard in Varnhold or from Edwyn) to get her to open up.
quests.outcome: Variel reveals she is one of Varan's Crownhost. Confirms Varan is alive and her MP signal comes from the direction of Vashkar. Agrees to travel with the player when ready.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player has not yet heard Varan's name (missed 1.7), Variel does not reveal anything this visit. The player must return after completing 1.7 or 1.11.

quests.name: Records of a Silent God
quests.gate: Completing 1.7 with the optional notice triggered, and returning to Edwyn alone after vespers [GATE]
quests.objective: Review the two sets of records with Edwyn — official and original. Identify the three discrepancies she has marked. Decide what to do with the information.
quests.outcome: Player has documentary proof the Silence was not a withdrawal. Edwyn asks them to take the copies somewhere safe. She will not leave Varnhold.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player does not return before leaving Varnhold, Edwyn destroys the copies in a panic two weeks later. The Lord Justiciar thread in Act 7 is permanently closed.

quests.name: A Templar's Failing
quests.gate: Completing 1.6 and a second meeting with Dava in Hallowmere [GATE — minimum relationship with Dava]
quests.objective: Convince Dava to let Syrael run an MP assessment on her. Travel with her to Tessara. Witness the assessment.
quests.outcome: Syrael's reading confirms external suppression of Dava's divine source. The three threads — records, theory of divine enslavement, failing Path — converge for the first time.
quests.failure_consequence: If Dava refuses, she can be approached once more after the player reaches Journeyman rank. A second refusal closes this thread permanently — the Act 1 conclusion still unlocks but with one fewer convergence point, weakening the case slightly.

quests.name: The Shape of a Secret
quests.gate: Completing 1.9, 1.11, and 1.12 [GATE — at least two of three required for minimum conclusion]
quests.objective: The three threads converge in Tessara. Variel, shown the evidence, confirms Varan is alive and contained in Vashkar. Aldra promotes the player to Journeyman.
quests.outcome: Act 2 unlocks. The strength of the conclusion (all three threads vs two) determines how much intel the player carries into Act 2 and which opening quests are pre-seeded.
quests.failure_consequence: With only two threads: the player enters Act 2 knowing Varan is in Vashkar but missing one piece of the picture. The first Act 2 quest compensates with a harder investigation variant.

quests.name: Into the Groves
quests.objective: Locate a missing survey team that went into the deep groves and did not return. The first contract in Sylvaren.
quests.outcome: Team found alive near an excavation site they stumbled on. The site is not a logging camp — systematic extraction, armed non-loggers arrived and told them to leave.
quests.failure_consequence: If the team is not found within the quest timer, one member dies. This reduces the witness testimony available in 2.4 but does not block the act.

quests.name: The Ranger's Map
quests.objective: Convince Elowen the player is not connected to the excavation. She tests the player — they must correctly answer a question about the survey team's findings from 2.1.
quests.outcome: Elowen shares her two-month excavation map: three sites near sealed elven ruins. She was told by the Grove-Warden to drop it. She did not.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player cannot answer Elowen's test (skipped 2.1), she walks away. The player must return after completing 2.1 — costs one quest slot.

quests.name: The Court of Seasons
quests.type: Character introduction — Queen Ilvariel (13) and Sylvaris Orenn (14)
quests.objective: Secure an audience with Queen Ilvariel using either the Charter commendation from Queen Maren or Sylvaris's intervention in the waiting hall.
quests.outcome: Ilvariel grants access to the sealed elven site and assigns two Silverbough Wardens. Sylvaris is established as the bridge between the player and the queen.
quests.failure_consequence: Without the commendation or Sylvaris's intervention, the audience is delayed by three in-game days. One Warden is assigned instead of two — slightly weaker support in 2.8.

quests.name: The Sealed Place
quests.objective: Enter the sealed elven site with Elowen and the Wardens. Document what was taken and find any traces of who took it.
quests.outcome: Ward components taken from a sealed Age of Dawn chamber. A dark elf merchant seal found on a discarded tool — House Vesh is connected.
quests.failure_consequence: If fewer witnesses survive from 2.1, one clue is missing. The House Vesh connection takes longer to confirm in 2.6.

quests.name: The Text That Should Not Exist
quests.gate: Completing 2.3 and minimum relationship with Sylvaris [GATE]
quests.objective: Read the original Age of Dawn text with Sylvaris in the Loremaster's vault. It describes divine enslavement as a theoretical act the Creator warned against: an enslaver with enough MP can apply the world's slavery system to a divine being, draining their MP while keeping them compliant through binding and pleasure.
quests.outcome: Player now understands what is being done to Varan — not a device or contract, but Kharrath himself, spending enormous MP to hold her. Sylvaris is visibly shaken.
quests.failure_consequence: Without this quest, the player knows Varan is captive but not the mechanism. Understanding the mechanism is what makes Act 8's liberation possible rather than just a rescue assault.

quests.name: House Vesh's Ledger
quests.objective: Meet Ilthuya in Veyrithil. She has already sent for the player. She lays her transaction ledger on the table: ten deals, all buyers now identifiable as Ember Conclave fronts.
quests.outcome: The Ember Conclave is named for the first time. Ilthuya provides a list of front organisations operating in Vashkar and Concord. She wants the Conclave gone — they used her house without her knowledge.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player arrives without the House Vesh seal from 2.4, Ilthuya is less forthcoming. She shares the Conclave name but not the full front list — one Act 4 investigation is harder.

quests.name: The Dimming Island
quests.gate: Completing 2.4 and 2.5 [GATE]
quests.objective: Trace the capture operation components from the Mossgate safehouse to a shipment heading to Khardun via Stonebridge. Race begins.
quests.outcome: Aeloria's island has been dimming for six weeks. The Archdruid and eldest elves have noticed. The race to intercept is now active.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player takes more than two in-game days to start this quest after 2.5, the shipment gets a head start and 2.8 has a harder intercept window.

quests.name: The Race to the Ward
quests.objective: Coordinate the intercept at Stonebridge. Player leads the Charter side, Ilvariel's Wardens handle the Sylvaren side.
quests.outcome: Shipment intercepted. Ward components destroyed. Aeloria's island brightens within hours. Both sides successful.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player arrives late (delayed in 2.7): the ward is 70% assembled. The intercept fight is harder and one component must be destroyed in a separate chase sequence. Still saveable but one Warden is injured and unavailable for Act 8.

quests.name: What Was Taken From Runeholm
quests.gate: Completing 2.8 [GATE]
quests.objective: Identify the copied Runeholm archive pages in the intercepted shipment. Send word to Runeholm — receive a reply requesting the player in person.
quests.outcome: Act 3 unlocks. Player now has: Ember Conclave named, Aeloria safe, and a trail leading to Khardun. Ilvariel's diplomatic endorsement letter is issued.

quests.name: Under the Mountain
quests.objective: Cross Stonebridge into Khardun. Register at the Hammerhall Charter post and pick up the standing contract for investigating the archive theft.
quests.outcome: Player enters dwarf culture: oaths, clan marks, and polite but firm suspicion of outsiders. Charter credentials grant limited access — Ilvariel's diplomatic letter helps.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Ilvariel's letter (missed in 2.9): Charter access is restricted to surface holds only. Several investigation shortcuts in 3.3 are unavailable.

quests.name: The Rune-Warden's Mother
quests.objective: Meet Sigrun at the Runeholm gate. Review the stolen pages and her mother's hidden notes from the spine of a family Deedbook.
quests.outcome: Stolen pages contain the assembly sequence for a ward targeting a stone-affinity MP being — Durgrim. Sigrun's mother noticed something wrong three years before she died. Her notes hint at a specific tunnel network.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player has Syrael's theory of divine enslavement from 1.9/2.5, they can cross-reference immediately. Without it, Sigrun must consult a colleague — costs one in-game day and delays 3.4.

quests.name: The Oathkeeper's Ledger
quests.objective: Track the thief through Runeholm's tunnel network using Sigrun's partial witness description. Identify the guild-runner who was paid by a Concord trade house front.
quests.outcome: Same front organisation name appears in Ilthuya's ledger from Act 2 — the chain is confirmed. The guild-runner has a Vashkar contact address.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Ilthuya's full front list (from 2.6 partial failure): the trade house front cannot be confirmed immediately. An extra investigation step is required in Goldenreach before 3.5 unlocks.

quests.name: Durgrim's Island
quests.gate: Completing 3.2 and 3.3 [GATE]
quests.objective: Run an MP assessment on the Great Anvil peak with Sigrun. Readings show early suppression — not yet a full ward but components assembling in the Goldenreach tunnels.
quests.outcome: Location of the assembly site confirmed. The Goldenreach thane must be notified discreetly — the assembly is on clan land and any heavy-handed approach will cause a diplomatic incident.
quests.failure_consequence: If the assessment is delayed more than three in-game days, the ward is further assembled and the 3.5 fight is harder.

quests.name: The Goldenreach Tunnel
quests.objective: Descend into the Goldenreach tunnel network. Destroy the partial capture assembly. Capture at least one mercenary for questioning.
quests.outcome: Assembly destroyed. Captured mercenary was hired through a Vashkar intermediary — the name Morvane appears for the first time. Durgrim's island stabilises.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player fails to capture a mercenary: Morvane's name does not appear here. It surfaces in Act 4 instead via Velindra's dossier, but the player enters Act 4 with one less piece of evidence.

quests.name: The Warmother's Omens
quests.type: Character introduction by correspondence — Ushara Ashfang (25)
quests.objective: Receive and reply to Ushara's message via the Charter relay. Establish contact. No travel required.
quests.outcome: Ushara notes she has been receiving omens she cannot interpret. The player's reply seeds the Act 5 relationship. A warm reply opens one additional dialogue option when meeting her in person.
quests.failure_consequence: Ignoring the message does not block Act 5 but Ushara's initial stance in 5.2 is cooler. The three-day assessment is harder.

quests.name: Sigrun's Oath
quests.gate: Completing 3.2 and minimum relationship with Sigrun [GATE]
quests.objective: Investigate the circumstances of the previous Rune-Warden's death. Trail leads to a forged accident report filed by the same guild-runner from 3.3.
quests.outcome: Sigrun's mother was killed because she got too close. Sigrun files a formal oath of investigation in the Durgrim Ledger — she is now personally committed and formally allies with the player. The dwarven coalition is fully secured.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player lacks evidence from 3.3 (extra step path), this quest is delayed to after 3.5. It still completes but Sigrun's oath arrives after the act climax rather than contributing to it.

quests.name: Red Stone City
quests.objective: Arrive at Cindergate via Toma Vey's ship. Register at the small Charter post. Take a contract introducing Vashkar's political landscape — a trade dispute between a demon House and a dark elf merchant.
quests.outcome: Player enters Vashkar culture: vivid, warm, politically sharp. Kharrath's Ember Temple dominates the skyline. House Morvane's estate is visible in the wealthier district.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Toma's ship (if she was not unlocked in Act 1): the player arrives via a slower route at higher cost. One Act 4 investigation shortcut is unavailable.

quests.name: The Duelist's Contract
quests.objective: Engage Velara Ash — the House Sarvoth duelist challenging Charter agents. Combat or negotiation both work. Win or negotiate well enough to earn her trust.
quests.outcome: Velara drops the pretense. She is watching for someone she can trust. Explains her fabricated contract and sister Sera trapped in Morvane's household. Needs Malvek's church to break it.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player loses the fight decisively: Velara does not open up this encounter. A second approach is available after the player completes one more Vashkar contract — costs one quest slot.

quests.name: The Envoy's Dossier
quests.objective: Attend the dinner at House Lysmere's Vashkar residence. Velindra presents her four-year dossier across three courses: Kharrath's behavioural changes, two missing Crownhost angels, unusual resource movements from the Ember Temple.
quests.outcome: Kharrath is named as the architect of the Silence for the first time. The player now has evidence connecting the god personally to the crime — not just his instruments.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player's Charter rank is below Veteran, Velindra is less forthcoming. She shares the behavioural changes but withholds the missing angel evidence — one piece of the dossier is missing until the player reaches Veteran rank.

quests.name: The Arbiter's Burden
quests.objective: Present Velindra's dossier to Grand Arbiter Iskara Thorne and request her help breaking Velara's fabricated contract. She needs one more piece: the original ward contract from 22 years ago.
quests.outcome: Iskara reveals her predecessor notarised an unusual sealed contract 22 years ago. She has always wondered about it. She now suspects she knows what it is and begins her own archive investigation.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Velindra's full dossier (from 4.3 partial): Iskara is unconvinced. A second meeting after 4.6 is required — delays Velara's contract resolution by one quest slot.

quests.name: Velara's Contract
quests.gate: Completing 4.2 and 4.4, minimum relationship with Velara [GATE]
quests.objective: Decide when Iskara voids the fabricated contract. Void now: Velara is freed immediately but Morvane is alerted. Wait: Sera remains at risk but the element of surprise is preserved.
quests.outcome: Velara is eventually freed either way. She provides the full Morvane estate layout and Ember Conclave internal structure. Her sister Sera's safety is affected by timing.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player voids immediately: Morvane accelerates her timetable. Quest 4.6 has a shorter window. If the player waits too long: Sera overhears something critical and Morvane has her reassigned to a different location — harder to extract in the sub-quest.

quests.name: The Ward for Thessaly
quests.gate: Completing 4.3 and 4.4 [GATE]
quests.objective: Cross-reference Velindra's dossier with Iskara's predecessor contract. Identify the Concord shipment carrying Thessaly's capture operation components. Travel to Concord.
quests.outcome: The shipment is confirmed: capture operation components for a being of hunt-and-wild-affinity MP — Thessaly. The race to intercept begins at Concord.
quests.failure_consequence: If Velara's contract was voided early (4.5 choice): Morvane diverts the shipment to a secondary route. The intercept in 4.7 is harder — requires Kiri's map from Act 5 (not yet available) or a harder Concord investigation.

quests.name: The Charter's Neutrality
quests.objective: Convince Charter Speaker Orsolya Dane to freeze the Concord shipment. She needs a legal override. Iskara Thorne can issue a Ledger Courts invalidation if the evidence is sufficient.
quests.outcome: Iskara issues the invalidation. The shipment is frozen. Thessaly's capture operation components are seized and destroyed. The Charter's neutrality is strained but holds.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player cannot produce sufficient evidence (partial dossier from 4.3): Orsolya refuses. The player must destroy the shipment covertly without Charter sanction — costs standing with the Concord Charter post.

quests.name: Malvek's Revelation
quests.gate: Completing 4.6 and 4.7 [GATE]
quests.objective: Iskara formally presents the predecessor contract to Malvek's church. The Hall of Ledgers officially turns against House Morvane. Every Morvane contract is under review.
quests.outcome: Thessaly is safe. The Ledger Courts are now coalition allies. Morvane's legal empire begins to crack. Kharrath knows the player is coming.
quests.failure_consequence: If the evidence is incomplete: Malvek's church suspends Morvane's contracts rather than formally opposing her. The Ledger Courts are neutral rather than allied in Act 8 — a weaker coalition position.

quests.name: The Tharos Road
quests.objective: Respond to Ushara Ashfang's intensified omens. Three clan shamans are seeing the same vision. Commit to coming to Tharos.
quests.outcome: Act 5 unlocks. Player's Veteran rank is confirmed. Ushara's message now includes the name of Wildmark as the meeting place.

quests.name: The Red Steppe
quests.objective: Arrive at Delta Market via Toma's ship or overland. Travel inland to Wildmark. Kharrath's battle-cult war-priests are active and the orc clans are visibly split.
quests.outcome: Player enters Tharos: hot, vast, politically fractured between old Thessaly traditions and the new battle-cult. Wildmark's Moot-Caller lodge is the destination.
quests.failure_consequence: If Toma Vey was not unlocked: overland arrival takes longer and costs more. One early Wildmark contact is unavailable on arrival.

quests.name: The Warmother
quests.type: Character introduction in person — Ushara Ashfang (25)
quests.objective: Present the full case to Ushara at Wildmark. She listens without reaction, then asks one question: what do you want from my clans? She gives the player three days to prove they understand Tharos.
quests.outcome: Ushara does not commit yet. She assigns Garet to guide the player for the three-day assessment.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player's reply to her correspondence (3.6) was cold or ignored: Ushara's three-day assessment has an extra challenge — she asks a second question before assigning Garet.

quests.name: The Clan Woman
quests.objective: Travel with Garet for three days. Resolve a grazing dispute between Clan Ironjaw and a beastfolk pack, and track a battle-cult war-priest operating in clan territory.
quests.outcome: Garet's manner thaws slightly. She mentions she was born in Marrowen without elaborating. The player may connect this to the Free Road thread from Act 1.
quests.failure_consequence: If the war-priest escapes: Clan Ironjaw's confidence in the player is reduced. Ushara's coalition commitment in 5.9 requires one additional condition — either defeating the war-priest later or producing the Thessaly salvage (if Act 4 was failed).

quests.name: The Map Broker
quests.objective: Negotiate with Kiri at Wildmark market. She wants information about what the Ember Conclave is actually doing in Tharos — she helped them once and needs to understand how badly she erred.
quests.outcome: The player gives Kiri what they know. She provides the full Ember Conclave supply route map through Tharos including the Wyrm Graves route. Her guilt is visibly genuine.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player has incomplete Conclave information (partial dossier from Act 4): Kiri's map is partial. The Wyrm Graves route is missing and must be found via Vael in 5.5 the hard way.

quests.name: The Graves of Wyrms
quests.objective: Cross into Fangwood. Convince Vael the player is not connected to the excavation by answering her question about sacred animal law. She leads the player to the site.
quests.outcome: The Wyrm Graves excavation site is larger than expected: a full Ember Conclave operation with Gilded Spears guards, extracting bones from a First Wyrm burial site.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player cannot answer Vael's sacred animal law question (skipped relevant world content): she requires the player to complete a secondary task first — drive off a group of poachers near the grove boundary.

quests.name: The Wyrm-Speaker
quests.objective: Find Ashkora after the ground shakes during the Wyrm Graves survey. Learn what she said to the excavation team.
quests.outcome: Ashkora told the workers that the one they woke is already awake and moving. She asks the player to come to the Scaled Peaks before acting on the site.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player ignores Ashkora and assaults the site immediately: the First Wyrm surfaces aggressively rather than peacefully in 5.7. The workers flee but one Warden and one Charter agent are injured.

quests.name: What the Wyrm Knows
quests.gate: Completing 5.6 and minimum relationship with Ashkora [GATE]
quests.objective: Be present for Ashkora's one-way communication with the First Wyrm in the Scaled Peaks. It is angry, old, and has been watching for three years. It decides the player is not part of the excavation.
quests.outcome: The First Wyrm surfaces at the Wyrm Graves the next day. It does not attack. Ember Conclave workers flee. Ward components left behind.
quests.failure_consequence: Without this quest: the player must assault the site with the workers still present — harder fight, more casualties, and the Wyrm surfaces mid-fight and may target anyone present indiscriminately.

quests.name: Hestrel's Ward
quests.gate: Completing 5.5 and 5.7 [GATE]
quests.objective: Access the abandoned Wyrm Graves assembly. Destroy the half-assembled capture operation using Sigrun's remote technical guidance via Charter relay. Vael and Garet provide ground support.
quests.outcome: the capture operation for Hestrel is destroyed. Her forge-fires stabilise. The coalition's logistics arm is secured.
quests.failure_consequence: If Sigrun is not an ally (Act 3 failure path): the player must improvise the destruction — there is a 40% chance one component survives and must be tracked down in a bonus chase sequence.

quests.name: The Warmother's Word
quests.gate: Completing 5.2, 5.8, minimum relationship with Ushara [GATE]
quests.objective: Accept Ushara's terms for coalition commitment. She asks one question: after this is done, will you help us recover what the loggers took from Fangwood? The player does not need to say yes — only to answer.
quests.outcome: Ushara commits Clan Ashfang, Clan Ironjaw, and Clan Redhorn to the Act 8 coalition. The Tharos coalition is fully secured.
quests.failure_consequence: If the war-priest escaped in 5.3 and the Thessaly salvage was not completed: Ushara commits Clan Ashfang only. Ironjaw and Redhorn require additional convincing in Act 7.

quests.name: The Supply Camp
quests.gate: Only available if Aeloria was enslaved in Act 2 [CONDITIONAL SALVAGE]
quests.objective: Help Elowen Ashbark (who went rogue after Act 2) destroy an Ember Conclave supply camp in Tharos. A dangerous two-person operation with no coalition backup.
quests.outcome: Partial Warden support restored for Act 8. Elowen formally re-joins the coalition. The Silverbough Wardens send a skeleton force rather than their full strength.

quests.name: The Battle-Cult Duel
quests.gate: Only available if Thessaly was enslaved in Act 4 [CONDITIONAL SALVAGE]
quests.objective: Challenge the battle-cult war-priest who commands Clans Ironjaw and Redhorn to a formal single combat under orc law.
quests.outcome: Victory flips Clans Ironjaw and Redhorn back to the coalition. Ushara's authority is restored. The Tharos coalition recovers to roughly 70% of full strength.

quests.name: The Dimming of Desire
quests.objective: Receive Velindra's urgent message about Nyxara's absence. Recognise the exact language used in 592 YC. Race to Emberspire begins. Board Toma's ship or find alternative passage.
quests.outcome: Reports confirmed: Nyxara has not given a public audience in six weeks. Her Mistress of Veils has issued a statement using the precise wording of the original Silence announcement.
quests.failure_consequence: If Toma was not unlocked: passage to Vashkar takes longer. Arrives with one fewer in-game day before the confrontation in 6.5 occurs.

quests.name: The Physician's Price
quests.objective: Meet Evara at the Gloamhaven guildhall. She will only share if satisfied the player intends to free Varan and not merely expose the truth.
quests.outcome: Evara describes a flaw in compliance-based captivity versus suppression: a goddess kept compliant rather than suppressed retains awareness and can send a faint outward signal if the compliance is interrupted for a moment. A being with foreign MP close enough can act as an anchor for that signal — enough to coordinate the liberation from outside and inside simultaneously.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player cannot satisfy Evara's condition (contradicted by prior choices suggesting power-seeking): she withholds the contact method from inside the captivity. The Act 8 rescue track becomes an assault — harder and with more casualties.

quests.name: Nyxara's Clergy
quests.objective: Speak to three junior Nyxara clergy in Emberspire without triggering the Ember Temple's notice. Gather their testimony about the cold altar.
quests.outcome: All three confirm Nyxara's private altar went cold eleven days ago — matching the date of the Ember Temple's closed ceremony.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player triggers Ember Temple notice during this quest: two of the three clergy refuse to speak. One testimony is enough for 6.5 but the evidence is weaker.

quests.name: Velindra's Warning
quests.gate: Completing 4.3 and minimum relationship with Velindra [GATE]
quests.objective: Reach Lady Velura Lysmere before she enters her Ember Temple meeting. Decide how much truth to reveal and how quickly.
quests.outcome: Velura goes still for a long time. Uses her diplomatic credentials to delay the summons by one week. House Lysmere's full diplomatic network remains available for Act 8.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player is too slow or fails the approach: Velura enters the meeting. She emerges politically neutralised — unable to act against Kharrath publicly. House Lysmere's network is removed from the Act 8 coalition.

quests.name: The Confrontation
quests.gate: Completing 6.3 and 6.4 [GATE]
quests.objective: Reconstruct what happened to Nyxara using the clergy testimony, Velindra's dossier, and Evara's knowledge. A witness saw two beings arguing in Kharrath's high sanctuary, then a blinding light, then silence.
quests.outcome: Confirmed: Nyxara is enslaved. The player arrives too late. This is the emotional gut-punch of the act. Kharrath moved the moment he decided to — the player's evidence-gathering could not prevent it.
quests.failure_consequence: There is no failure state here. The outcome is fixed. What varies is how much evidence the player carries into Act 7 and Act 8 based on what they gathered in this act.

quests.name: What Evara Knows
quests.gate: Completing 6.2 and minimum relationship with Evara [GATE]
quests.objective: Return to Evara with the confirmation. Receive her full briefing on the liberation method from the inside. Evara commits to being present at Ashvault.
quests.outcome: Player now has the rescue method for Act 8. Without this quest the rescue track is unavailable — Act 8 becomes confrontation-only with the coalition handling Ashvault as a straight assault.
quests.failure_consequence: If the player failed to satisfy Evara in 6.2: this quest does not exist. Evara will not share. Rescue track in Act 8 is locked.

quests.name: The Faith in Pieces
quests.objective: Return to Aldermere. Open Hand hospitals are overwhelmed. Crown Basilica in Varnhold is holding emergency councils. Urgent message from Princess Lysa Voss is waiting in Solhaven.
quests.outcome: Player re-enters familiar territory changed by the act of revealing the Conclave's name publicly (if the player did so). Solhaven feels different depending on prior choices.

quests.name: Lysa's Discovery
quests.gate: Completing 1.8 and minimum relationship with Princess Lysa [GATE]
quests.objective: Review the sealed 592 YC diplomatic correspondence between Aurendale and a Morvane representative in the royal archive with Lysa. It arrives two weeks before the Silence.
quests.outcome: Closes the political timeline. Lysa formally commits to the player's case before the Diet of Crowns. Her backing is what makes the Lord Justiciar's public retraction politically viable.
quests.failure_consequence: Without Lysa's backing: the Lord Justiciar retracts only to a closed council session rather than publicly. The Silence reveal is quieter and has less political impact. Moves toward the Silent Victory ending.

quests.name: The Seeker's Ritual
quests.type: Sister Ezan full appearance — permanent choice
quests.objective: Meet Sister Ezan in Solhaven. She shows the reconstructed ritual. Permanent choice: help her complete it properly (Secret End available) or suppress it (Secret End permanently closed).
quests.outcome: If helped: Ezan begins final preparations. The Secret End is now available contingent on the True End path in Act 8. If suppressed: Ezan disappears and the Seekers scatter — the Secret End is gone.
quests.failure_consequence: There is no failure state — only the binary choice. The choice cannot be undone.

quests.name: Solenne's Silence
